title: Normal proper completion with divisorial boundary
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. All schemes are separated and of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism], where separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Integral means reduced and irreducible [def-pc-integral-scheme]; normal means that all local rings are integrally closed domains. Dimensions are topological Krull dimensions [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $Y$ be smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], connected [def-weil-connected-scheme], nonempty and not proper over $k$. Then $Y$ is integral and there exist a normal integral proper $k$-scheme $X_0$ and a dense open immersion $j_0:Y\hookrightarrow X_0$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. The reduced complement $E_0=X_0\setminus j_0(Y)$ is nonempty, and every irreducible component of $E_0$ has dimension $\dim Y-1$. In particular $\dim X_0=\dim Y$ is a positive finite integer.

source.place: Proposition 8.25, p.154, referred rational-action proof: Milne (2013), Proposition 4.1 proof, first paragraph (embed, blow up the boundary, normalize), and Aside 5.4 (Nagata can replace quasi-projectivity). Local article WANTED; read https://arxiv.org/html/1311.6060v2. The normal divisorial-completion combination has no single Stacks tag.

proof.text: For every finite-type $k$-scheme $Z$ used below, choose a finite affine cover $\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ with $A_i$ finitely generated over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. By [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components], each $A_i$ is Noetherian and each affine space is topologically Noetherian. A descending chain of closed subsets of $Z$ stabilizes on each member of this finite cover, hence stabilizes on $Z$. Thus $Z$ is locally Noetherian and its topology is Noetherian. In particular every open in $Z$ is quasi-compact: otherwise finite unions of members of an open cover would have no maximal member, contradicting stabilization of ascending chains of opens.

source.place: Tag 01T6, lemma-finite-type-noetherian; affine argument and finite-cover assembly

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-smooth-geometrically-normal] to the smooth structure morphism of $Y$, using the trivial field extension: $Y$ is normal and reduced. By [lem-trf-normal-topologically-noetherian-components] and step 1, its irreducible components are a finite disjoint union of open and closed integral schemes. Since $Y$ is connected and nonempty, exactly one component occurs. Hence $Y$ is integral.

Apply [thm-nagata-compactification] to $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Its separatedness and finite type are hypotheses, and $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated. By [def-nagata-compactifiable] and [def-nagata-compactification], obtain an open immersion $Y\hookrightarrow P$ with $P$ proper over $k$. No quasi-projectivity of $Y$ is required.

source.place: Tag 0F41, theorem-nagata, applied over a field

proof.text: Let $T$ be the reduced induced closed subscheme on $\overline{|Y|}\subseteq P$, supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Its topology is irreducible, being the closure of the irreducible set $|Y|$, and it is reduced, so $T$ is integral. Over the open subscheme $Y$ its defining ideal is zero: the affine description in that node gives the nilradical on every affine open of $Y$, which is zero by step 2. Therefore $Y\hookrightarrow P$ factors as a dense open immersion into $T$, with its original scheme structure. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper], $T$ is proper over $k$, hence finite type. Step 1 applies to $T$.

Use [lemma-nagata-qc-open-complement-ideal-exists] on the qcqs scheme $T$ and its quasi-compact open $Y$, obtaining a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I$ with $V(\mathcal I)=T\setminus Y$. Apply [det-nagata-boundary-divisor-cartier]: the blowup $b:B=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}T\to T$ is a $Y$-admissible blow-up [def-nagata-admissible-blowup], so by [lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-over-open] the induced morphism $b^{-1}(Y)=B\times_TY\to Y$ is an isomorphism and $Y$ is identified with the open $b^{-1}(Y)\subseteq B$; moreover $\mathcal I\mathcal O_B$ defines an effective Cartier divisor $D$ with support $B\setminus Y$. The ideal is nonzero since it is the unit ideal over nonempty $Y$. Thus [lem-sfb-integral-blowup-projective-geometry] gives integrality of $B$. By [lemma-nagata-blowup-proper] and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition], $B$ is proper over $k$. In particular $B$ is finite type, so step 1 applies.

source.place: Tag 02OS, lemma-blowing-up-gives-effective-Cartier-divisor; Tag 02ND, lemma-blow-up-integral-scheme; properties.tex Tag 01PH, lemma-quasi-coherent-finite-type-ideals

proof.text:
Let $
u:X_0=B^
u	o B$ be the function-field normalization [def-sc-normalization]. Since $B$ is integral, this is also its componentwise normalization [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization]. By [lem-sfb-componentwise-normalization-generic-properties], $X_0$ is normal and has exactly one irreducible-component generic point. By [lem-sc-normalization-exists], $
u$ is finite and birational, and $X_0$ is proper over $k$, hence finite type. Step 1 and [lem-trf-normal-topologically-noetherian-components] then make $X_0$ a finite disjoint union of integral components; exactly one occurs, so it is integral. Since the open $Y\subseteq B$ is normal, [lem-sc-normalization-over-normal-locus] identifies $
u^{-1}Y$ with $Y$. This gives an open immersion $j_0:Y\hookrightarrow X_0$, dense because a nonempty open subset of an irreducible space is dense.

proof.text: The extended ideal $\mathcal I\mathcal O_{X_0}$ is effective Cartier. Indeed, on an affine open of $B$ where $D$ has equation $t$, the element $t$ is nonzero in the common function field. The normalization [def-sc-normalization] is built from subrings of that field, so the image of $t$ remains nonzero. Since $X_0$ is integral, multiplication by this image is injective on each local ring; this is precisely [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. These local equations generate the extended ideal and have vanishing set $\nu^{-1}|D|$: a local ring homomorphism sends a local equation into the target maximal ideal exactly when it belongs to the source maximal ideal. Hence the resulting divisor $D_0$ has support $X_0\setminus j_0(Y)$.

source.place: Tag 02OO, lemma-pullback-effective-Cartier-defined (2), elementary local-equation proof in this birational case

proof.text: Give $E_0=X_0\setminus j_0(Y)$ its reduced induced closed structure using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Its support equals $|D_0|$ by step 7. It is nonempty: otherwise the open immersion $j_0$ would be surjective and therefore an isomorphism [def-weil-open-immersion], making $Y$ proper, contrary to hypothesis. By [lem-sc-dimension-locally-algebraic], $\dim X_0=\dim Y=:d$, and every nonempty affine open of $X_0$ has dimension $d$ and dimension $d$ at each of its points. By [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], $d$ is finite; it is nonnegative since $Y$ is nonempty.

Let $C$ be any irreducible component of $E_0$ and $\xi$ its generic point. Choose an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X_0$ of $\xi$ on which $D_0$ has a single equation $t$. It can be chosen as a principal refinement of a finite-type affine chart, so $A$ is a finitely generated $k$-algebra and is Noetherian by step 1. It is a domain since $X_0$ is integral, and $t\ne0$ by step 7. The prime $\mathfrak p$ of $\xi$ is minimal over $(t)$: otherwise a smaller prime containing $t$ would give a proper irreducible closed subset inclusion $C\subsetneq C'\subseteq |D_0|$ after taking closure, contradicting maximality of $C$. By [lem-sfb-krull-principal-ideal-height-bound], $\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak p\le1$. Since $t\in\mathfrak p$ is nonzero, the strict chain $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak p$ gives the opposite bound. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime], $\dim A_{\mathfrak p}=1$.

source.place: Tag 0BCN, lemma-effective-Cartier-codimension-1 (2), specialized to the integral case; algebra.tex Tag 00KV, lemma-minimal-over-1 (1), and Tag 00KF, definition-height

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-local-ring-trdeg] to the finite-type algebra $A$ and prime $\mathfrak p$ of step 9. Step 8 gives $\dim_{\mathfrak p}(\operatorname{Spec}A)=d$, and step 9 gives $\dim A_{\mathfrak p}=1$, so $d=1+\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. The residue field is the residue field of $X_0$ at $\xi$, since open restriction preserves the local ring. By [lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg] applied to the nonempty irreducible closed subset $C\subseteq X_0$, its dimension is that same transcendence degree. Thus $\dim C=d-1$. This holds for every component. Since $E_0$ is nonempty it has such a component, whose dimension is nonnegative. Therefore $d\ge1$, proving the positive-dimension assertion as well.
